comparison: Both strongly support the UPOAO model development and blood flow interruption validation (C15-C18, C74). OpenEval emphasizes methodology and multi-modal imaging validation, while peer reviewers praise the 'clear demonstration of the surgery procedure' and 'solid data.' Complete agreement on model validity.

Both support the dose-response comparison (C19, C20, C25, C75). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of 30 vs 60 min ischemia across multiple endpoints. Peer reviewers confirm 'convincing histological and in vivo data' for time course changes. OpenEval covers broader claim set including ERG data (C21-C24) not explicitly mentioned in peer R2.

Partial overlap on ERG functional data (C21-C24). OpenEval R2 addresses dose-response including ERG b-waves and OPs. Peer R3 confirms ERG findings and notes similarity to human RAO patterns (C80-C81), adding clinical relevance dimension not in OpenEval R2.

Perfect agreement on temporal retinal structural changes (C26-C31, C76). Both support OCT and histological data showing layer-specific effects with inner retina preferentially affected. OpenEval provides technical detail while peer review confirms 'convincing histological and in vivo data.'

Complete agreement on biphasic GCL thickness hypothesis (C32-C33). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes direct edema measurement would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers accept the mechanistic interpretation without challenge, noting it aligns with established ischemia-reperfusion pathophysiology.

Both support bipolar cell pathology findings (C34-C37). OpenEval emphasizes PKCα immunostaining and ERG b-wave correlation. Peer R6 covers broader inner retinal cell types including HCs and amacrine cells (C38-C42), with overlapping support for BC data.

Both support outer retina preservation (C38). OpenEval notes consistency with choroidal blood supply anatomy. Peer R6 includes this within broader assessment of retinal cell survival data, confirming differential vulnerability patterns.

Both support HC and cholinergic amacrine cell degeneration (C39-C42). OpenEval provides detailed temporal and morphological analysis. Peer R6 encompasses these findings within comprehensive validation of 'retinal neuronal cell survivals' across multiple cell types.

Divergent evaluations of leukocyte migration claims (C43-C46). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation requiring experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting transcriptomic inference as consistent with later immunostaining data showing CD45+ cells.

Complete agreement on oxidative stress and mitochondrial pathway enrichment at 3 days (C47-C50). Both support GO analysis findings. OpenEval notes consistency with IRI mechanisms, peer reviewers accept within temporal progression narrative from ischemia to oxidative stress to inflammation.

Both strongly support immune inflammatory response at 7 days (C51-C54). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of GO enrichment, hub gene analysis, and RT-qPCR validation. Peer reviewers explicitly validate 'sequential event' including neuroinflammation leading to cell death.

Divergent evaluations of oxidative stress-to-inflammation mechanistic link (C55-C56). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to small gene overlap and inferential nature. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the temporal progression as coherent pathological narrative without challenge.

Strong agreement on immune cell infiltration and activation (C58-C62, C77). OpenEval emphasizes quantification and morphological changes. Peer reviewers explicitly validate 'reperfusion-induced leukocyte infiltration' and 'microglial activation' as part of sequential pathological events.

Both support UPOAO vs HIOP comparison showing shared immune responses but distinct metabolic signatures (C65-C69, C78). OpenEval notes functional validation would strengthen metabolic claims. Peer reviewers confirm comparison provides 'informative evidence to differentiate these models' and supports clinical relevance.

Complete agreement on UCCAO vs UPOAO differences (C70-C73, C110). Both support conclusion that UCCAO models different pathological process (chronic hypoperfusion vs acute ischemia). OpenEval emphasizes minimal gene overlap and distinct pathways; peer reviewers confirm transcriptomic comparison differentiates models.

Both support clinical relevance through similarity to human RAO patterns (C80-C81). OpenEval R15 covers broader clinical validation including anatomical damage patterns (C82-C84). Peer R3 confirms ERG similarity to human RAO strengthens translational validity.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic model integrating cellular, transcriptomic, and immunological findings (C97-C98). OpenEval notes causal relationships would benefit from interventional studies. Peer reviewers explicitly validate 'sequential event' connecting oxidative stress, immune activation, and neuronal death.

Both support UPOAO vs HIOP phenotypic comparison (C99-C101). OpenEval covers broader claim set including molecular differences (C102-C104) and notes mechanistic interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers confirm comparison differentiates models and supports UPOAO specificity for retinal artery occlusion.

Both support UCCAO's distinct epigenetic signature (C105-C109). OpenEval emphasizes m6A-related genes and notes inferential conclusions require validation. Peer reviewers accept transcriptomic comparison as differentiating UCCAO from acute ischemia models without challenge.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C112-C114, C79, C111). Both support comprehensive characterization and model validity. OpenEval notes therapeutic screening utility remains prospective. Peer reviewers enthusiastically endorse model as 'novel tool' that 'will certainly inspire further investigation.'

Both support leukocyte infiltration mechanisms (C85-C87, C86). OpenEval emphasizes established literature framework with citations. Peer R10 validates infiltration findings through immunostaining data showing CD45+ cells as part of sequential pathological events.

OpenEval R21 synthesizes IRI literature (C88-C96) to interpret UPOAO findings, rating SUPPORTED but noting mechanisms are inferential. Peer R13 validates the mechanistic narrative connecting oxidative stress, immune activation, and neuronal death as coherent and accepted.

Both address methodological details (C115-C117). OpenEval notes male-only mice limitation restricts generalizability. Peer reviewers do not explicitly critique this limitation, focusing instead on overall methodological quality and surgical procedure clarity.

Peer R16 supports background/rationale claims (C1-C14) establishing need for new model. No corresponding OpenEval result addresses these contextual claims, as OpenEval focused on evaluating experimental findings rather than background literature.
